items.title: Tyner McCoy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I mentioned Debussy, Ravel, and Stravinsky... I didn't get too involved in the concepts of some of the composers... I didn't want my music to stretch in that direction.

ctx.x: Yeah, I haven’t tried that one yet (both laugh).

Go in and de-tune the piano while you’re playing. But when somebody says, “Oh, McCoy Tyner”--as I was talking to Dr. Leonard Brown and he says, “well you know you put on any record and if it has Tyner on it, you are going to know within the first two or three notes.” You know it’s Tyner because of his touch, because of his approach to sound, his approach to the piano, but that’s why I asked you so much about your early training. There was a series, I’m sure you are familiar with it, Steve Rowland did the five…
